The assert expects a single total of 14, so this version returns the sum of all digits across the list. The team note asks for a per-number list like `[1, 2, 11]`, which would fail that assert. I followed the assert. If you want the per-number version, it would be `[sum(int(d) for d in str(abs(n))) for n in numbers]`.

```python
def sum_of_digits(numbers):
    return sum(int(d) for n in numbers for d in str(abs(n)))

assert sum_of_digits([10, 2, 56]) == 14
```

CONFIDENCE: 90
